one_liner: Code hosting platform with APIs for repos, issues, PRs, Actions, and more.

evidence.claim: Authentication uses tokens (personal access token, GitHub App token, or GITHUB_TOKEN) sent in the Authorization header
evidence.quote: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` in a GitHub Actions workflow.

evidence.claim: OAuth2 is supported via OAuth apps, though GitHub Apps are recommended
evidence.quote: You can also create an OAuth token with an OAuth app to access the REST API. However, GitHub recommends that you use a GitHub App instead.

evidence.claim: Tokens are passed as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header
evidence.quote: In most cases, you can use `Authorization: Bearer` or `Authorization: token` to pass a token.

evidence.claim: GitHub also offers a GraphQL API alongside REST
evidence.quote: The GitHub GraphQL API offers more precise and flexible queries than the GitHub REST API.

evidence.claim: GitHub ships an official MCP server from its own GitHub org
evidence.quote: The GitHub MCP Server connects AI tools directly to GitHub's platform. This gives AI agents, assistants, and chatbots the ability to read repositories and code

notes: Free tier exists (docs header: 'Version: Free, Pro, & Team'); PATs and OAuth app registration are self-serve from any free account. REST API is fully OpenAPI-described and spans dozens of resource groups (Actions, Activity, Pulls, Issues, etc.) — well over 50 endpoints. Org resources may require SAML SSO token authorization or admin-granted GitHub App installation, but core developer access is ungated. Official MCP server lives in the github/github-mcp-server repo.
